newsitem.title: FRANCE: French president endorses UNESCO bioethics accord.
newsitem.headline: French president endorses UNESCO bioethics accord.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac endorsed on Thursday the work of a special UNESCO committee drafting a global accord on ethical guidelines for genetic research.

"The draft Declaration on the Human Genome and Human Rights that you have drawn up is the very symbol of ethical reflection," Chirac told UNESCO's International Bioethics Committee as it began a two-day meeting in Paris.
The panel of 55 experts from 40 countries include doctors and scientists as well as philosophers and lawyers. They will vote on Friday whether to approve the draft.

UNESCO director-general Federico Mayor, also speaking at the comittee's opening session, said the initiative aimed "to guarantee respect for the rights and freedom of the human person in a context where unprecedented developments in human genetics are raising legitimate concern".
Panel members said they hoped the accord would foster scientific progress while preventing human rights abuses and protecting public health.

The six-page draft declaration recognises that human genetics research holds vast potential but warns that the research must be regulated "to guard against any eugenic practice that runs counter to human dignity and human rights".

Stating that the genetic material found in each and every human cell is "the common heritage of humanity", it cautions that peoples' genetic makeup should never be used as a basis for granting or denying their rights.
UNESCO -- the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation -- created the IBC in 1993 to monitor developing ethical issues in genetic research and engineeering.

The panel hopes the declaration will be adopted by UNESCO member states -- and thus turned into an international convention -- in time for the 50th anniversary of the U.N. Universal Declaration of Human Rights in 1998.
